source_overlay.purpose: Prepare 0.84.2 without changing the pending 0.84.1 source or final artifacts.

scope: Lower proven launch, loader and driver/protocol metadata-reader stack peaks. No ABI or cache/read-policy change.

workspaces.initialization: Copy Source identity directly and initialize cache metadata in the final allocation. Cached bytes remain MaybeUninit until filled.
workspaces.lifetime: Per classify/load/metadata probe; drop only after synchronous callback/read returns. Launch reader closes before child publication/execution.

workspaces.initialization: One resident allocation; initialize each original record at its final address, no whole-array temporary.
workspaces.lifetime: Library scan through complete dependency resolution. Entries only own copied metadata; loaded images and module leases keep separate original owners.

ownership.admission: Short RuntimeGuard only around exact task_context::enter/leave. No owner held across heap or filesystem work. Admitted unwind token protects allocation, use and acknowledged release across waits/migration.
ownership.allocation_failure: No guard constructed without admitted token and nonnull allocation. Allocation failure returns the token and the existing failure form (None/false or launch error -8). Library-active publication follows successful workspace acquisition.
ownership.early_return: Lexical scratch owner releases on malformed headers, rejected metadata, read failure and ordinary cancellation returns. Reservation/completion rollback remains the existing exact-generation owner.
ownership.release_failure: Nonzero heap acknowledgement is a terminal invariant failure; original unwind token remains pinned and normal completion is not published.
ownership.constraints: Scratch contains plain temporary data with no destructors/external resource ownership; no Send/Sync implementation. No lock spans I/O.

caller_and_nested_stack.path: launch::classify / launch::run -> metadata / image load -> cached module reader -> filesystem
caller_and_nested_stack.context: R4X caller with its own dynamic stack contract, or fixed 64-KB kernel/async worker. Callee and IRQ stack needs remain additional; fixed frames are not whole-task high-water measurements.
caller_and_nested_stack.reduction: Remove the 9208-byte reader from the caller frame before every nested file read; keep only small pointer/guard metadata.

caller_and_nested_stack.context: Initial discovery uses the BSP bootstrap stack before runtime; later inspection runs on its admitted task. Caller retains its 2048-byte metadata output. BSP reserve is not inferred from the independent 64-KB task allocation.
caller_and_nested_stack.reduction: Metadata probe fixed frame 9384 -> 200 bytes; R4D/R4P inline caller frame is not separately emitted and is not counted as zero.

caller_and_nested_stack.path: mod_load_libraries -> probe -> metadata reader -> filesystem; later resolve_pending recursion
caller_and_nested_stack.context: Linear BSP loader startup. Pending set lives through both scan and dependency recursion; no single task high-water is claimed.
caller_and_nested_stack.reduction: At nested probe entry, fixed outer+inner frames 51776 -> 5168 bytes, excluding return addresses and deeper calls. resolve_pending remains 264 bytes per level; runtime fixed library limit is unchanged.

temporary_image_context.reason: The first private image used the canonical kernel version in its installation manifest; image verification rejected it. The existing image builder now receives an isolated path/version context matching the candidate.

limits: Static frames exclude return addresses, nested callees and IRQ state; they are not runtime stack high-water measurements.
Existing 64-KB kernel task stacks and per-module memory budgets are unchanged.
No physical OOM, forced release-failure or new whole-module test campaign; failure ownership and token return were reviewed at each actual branch.
Windows host and physical hardware were not exercised.
performance_assessment: Overall 100.688431 versus 96.871935 in 0.84.1. Filesystem score 98.379360 versus 85.405707: the earlier large filesystem observation was not repeated. Lifecycle elapsed ns/op decreased about 2.53%; memory about 5.77%; scheduler/IPC increased about 1.64/1.71%. One mandatory run per release is not a statistical/cause-isolated speedup proof; static stack reductions are independently proven. No speed budget or extra timing campaign.
